The error confirms it: `qml-module-qtmultimedia` on your system is the **Qt5** version, but this theme (`pixel-munchlax`) declares `QtVersion=6` and uses unversioned imports (`import QtQuick`, `import QtMultimedia`) — which is Qt6-style syntax. Qt5's QML engine requires explicit version numbers (`import QtQuick 2.15`), hence "Library import requires a version."

Let me confirm which `sddm-greeter` binary is actually installed/running.

lastPrompt: Why does my sddm theme not work?

content.text:
Confirmed root cause: your system's `sddm` package (v0.20.0, Ubuntu) is linked against **Qt5** (`libQt5Quick.so.5`, etc.), but `pixel-munchlax`'s `Main.qml` uses unversioned imports like `import QtQuick` — that's Qt6 syntax. Qt5's QML engine requires a version on every import (`import QtQuick 2.15`), so it throws "Library import requires a version." There's also no Qt6 QML runtime installed at all on this box, so even fixing the version numbers wouldn't get you `Qt5Compat.GraphicalEffects` reliably paired with a Qt6 theme — this theme fundamentally targets a Qt6 SDDM build, which Ubuntu's `sddm` package here isn't.

Your two realistic options:

questions.question: How do you want to fix this? pixel-munchlax needs Qt6 SDDM, but your system has Qt5 SDDM (0.20.0 from Ubuntu repos) with no Qt6 QML runtime installed.

options.label: Switch to a Qt5-compatible theme
options.description: Use 'maya' (already installed) or 'simple-sddm' (already cloned to /usr/share/sddm/themes/, check if it's Qt5) — just update /etc/sddm.conf.d/theme.conf's Current= line. Fast, no system changes.

options.label: Install sddm-git / Qt6 SDDM
options.description: Ubuntu doesn't ship a Qt6 sddm package by default; would need a PPA or building from source, plus qt6-declarative and QtMultimedia6 QML modules. More work, higher risk of breaking your login manager.

options.label: Just diagnose further, don't change anything yet
options.description: I've identified the cause; you'll decide what to do on your own.

lastPrompt: Why does my sddm theme not work?

content.text:
Before touching anything, here's the concrete situation and plan:

**Why this is nontrivial:** Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) ships `sddm 0.20.0` built against **Qt5** in its own repos — there is no Qt6 `sddm` package in Ubuntu's official archives for noble. You also have `kde-config-sddm 5.27` installed, meaning your desktop itself is **Plasma 5**, not Plasma 6. Getting Qt6 SDDM here means either:

1. **Add the `kubuntu-ppa/backports` PPA** (the standard source for Qt6-built `sddm` on Ubuntu 24.04) and upgrade the `sddm` package + pull in `qt6-declarative`, `qml6-module-qt5compat-graphicaleffects`, `qml6-module-qtmultimedia`, etc. Risk: this PPA also carries newer Qt6 libs that can affect other packages via dependency resolution, and mixing a Plasma-5 desktop with a Qt6-only display manager is not a combination Kubuntu tests for — if anything goes wrong you could be dropped to a broken login screen (recoverable via TTY: Ctrl+Alt+F3, then `sudo systemctl restart sddm` or reverting `theme.conf`).
2. **Build `sddm` from source against Qt6** yourself — much more work, more moving parts, same end risk, no benefit over (1) on this system.

Given the risk profile (this controls your actual graphical login), I want explicit confirmation before I add a third-party PPA and upgrade your display manager package. Do you want me to proceed with option 1 (add `kubuntu-ppa/backports`, install Qt6 `sddm` + required QML modules)?

questions.question: Proceed with adding the kubuntu-ppa/backports PPA and upgrading sddm + Qt6 QML modules to get pixel-munchlax working? This changes your system login manager and pulls in third-party packages.

options.label: Yes, proceed
options.description: Add ppa:kubuntu-ppa/backports, apt update, install/upgrade sddm + qt6-declarative + qml6-module-qt5compat-graphicaleffects + qtmultimedia6 QML modules. I'll verify sddm still starts before finishing.

options.label: No, switch to Qt5-compatible theme instead (Recommended)
options.description: Much lower risk: point /etc/sddm.conf.d/theme.conf at 'maya' (already installed) or check if simple-sddm supports Qt5, no system package changes, reversible in seconds.

options.label: Stop here, I'll decide later
options.description: You have the diagnosis; don't make any changes yet.
